neighbours.label: the piece right after un- in a split word: un|acc|ustomed, un|cer|emonious, un|ce|asing; the same stem without un- stays quiet
fire: The visitors found the local customs strange and unaccustomed.
He gave the old sofa an unceremonious shove out the door.
An unceasing wind blew across the plain all winter.
Her unaccustomed silence worried the whole family.
The manager was dismissed in an unceremonious way.
The unceasing noise of traffic kept me awake.
Unequal pay remains a problem in many industries.
They felt unaccustomed joy at the sight of land.
quiet: The visitors found the local customs strange and charming.
He gave the old sofa a gentle push out the door.
A steady wind blew across the plain all winter.
Her accustomed silence comforted the whole family.
The manager was dismissed after a formal ceremony.
The ceaseless noise of traffic kept me awake.
Equal pay remains a goal in many industries.
They were accustomed to the sight of land.
